name: CloudFox - AWS Post-Exploitation Enumeration
description: CloudFox helps attackers find exploitable attack paths in AWS using existing credentials. It answers offensive questions: what roles can I assume, which secrets/env vars hold credentials, what public endpoints and instances exist, where can I move laterally, and what permissions do I have. Read-only enumeration that surfaces privilege-escalation and lateral-movement opportunities.
notes:
=== PREREQ: configured AWS creds ===
  aws configure --profile <profile>     # or env vars / assumed role
  aws sts get-caller-identity --profile <profile>   # confirm identity

=== RUN EVERYTHING ===
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> all-checks
  # Across all enabled regions by default; outputs CSV/loot to ./cloudfox-output/

=== TARGETED CHECKS ===
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> inventory        # what exists, where
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> endpoints        # reachable URLs/APIs
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> instances        # EC2 + IPs
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> secrets          # Secrets Manager/SSM
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> env-vars         # creds in task/lambda env
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> iam-simulator    # what can my principal do
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> permissions      # enumerate IAM perms
  cloudfox aws --profile <profile> principals        # users/roles

=== LOOT FILES (ready-to-run commands) ===
  # cloudfox writes loot/ with pre-built aws cli + pmapper/pacu follow-ups

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Pacu              # full exploitation framework
  enumerate-iam     # quick permission brute
  ScoutSuite/Prowler # audit (defensive framing)
  pmapper           # IAM privesc graphing

recommended.note: Pacu for active exploitation after CloudFox mapping.
Prowler/ScoutSuite give the defensive audit view.

defense.why_it_works: CloudFox calls read-only AWS APIs (Describe*, List*, Get*) permitted by the compromised principal. These calls are normal control-plane activity, so enumeration blends in unless volume/patterns are baselined.
defense.prerequisites: Valid AWS credentials (keys, assumed role, or instance profile).
defense.impact: Rapid discovery of privilege-escalation paths, exposed secrets, reachable endpoints, and lateral-movement options.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1526/T1580] CloudTrail burst of Describe*/List*/Get* across many services and regions from one identity in a short window; cloudfox user-agent; SimulatePrincipalPolicy calls.
defense.artifacts: CloudTrail enumeration spikes; GetSecretValue/GetParameter reads; aws-sdk-go user agent patterns.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail (eventName=Describe* OR eventName=List* OR eventName=Get*)
| stats dc(eventSource) as services count by userIdentity.arn
| where services > 10 AND count > 200
defense.sentinel_kql:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventName startswith "Describe" or EventName startswith "List" or EventName startswith "Get"
| summarize Services=dcount(EventSource), Calls=count() by UserIdentityArn, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Services > 10 and Calls > 200
defense.prevention: Least-privilege IAM; do not store secrets in env vars/user-data (use short-lived creds); GuardDuty (Recon finding types); alert on cross-service enumeration bursts; scope roles tightly.

detections.name: AWS cross-service enumeration burst (CloudFox/Pacu)
detections.logic:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail (eventName=Describe* OR eventName=List* OR eventName=Get* OR eventName=SimulatePrincipalPolicy)
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(eventSource) as services count by _time, userIdentity.arn
| where services > 10 AND count > 200
detections.false_positives: CSPM tools, inventory automation, backup scanners
detections.tuning: Baseline per-identity service breadth; allowlist known automation roles
